t: Umayyad claimants seize Damascus
c: Two Umayyads, Abu al-Umaytir al-Sufyani and Maslama ibn Ya'qub, successively seized control of Damascus from 811 to 813, and declared themselves caliphs.

t: Umar II's policies reversed, rebellions ensue
c: After his death in 720, his policies were largely reversed, resulting in rebellions.

c: Gil González Dávila set out from the Caribbean island of Hispaniola early in 1524, with the intention of exploring the Caribbean coast of Nicaragua.

c: In 1628 the towns of the Manche Chʼol were placed under the administration of the governor of Verapaz, with Francisco Morán as their ecclesiastical head.

c: Kowoj and Itza leaders in these mission towns rebelled against their Spanish overlords in 1704, but although well-planned, the rebellion was quickly crushed.

t: Columbus discovers the Americas
c: Christopher Columbus discovered the Americas for the Kingdom of Castile and León in 1492.

c: Spanish conquistador Pedro de Alvarado passed through Soconusco with a sizeable force in 1523, en route to conquer Guatemala.

t: Soconusco pacified by Alvarado

t: Soconusco transferred to Audiencia Real of Guatemala
c: In 1556, Soconusco passed into the jurisdiction of the Audiencia Real of Guatemala, with independent governors appointed by the Crown.

t: Luis Marín leads reconnaissance expedition into Chiapas
c: In 1524 Luis Marín led a small party on a reconnaissance expedition into Chiapas.

t: Chiapa transferred from New Spain to Guatemala
c: Highland Chiapas, known as Chiapa, fell under the jurisdiction of New Spain until 1530, when it was transferred to Guatemala.

t: Coxoh Maya conquered by Spanish forces
c: The Coxoh Maya, who inhabited a small area along the San Gregorio River between Comitán and the Guatemalan border, were probably conquered in 1528.

t: Last Long Count date inscribed at Toniná
